answer: River-gauge cipher: one $18 ultrasonic level sensor per identity, bolted to a real riverbank. Each epoch the agent reads its river level, derives a cipher from that reading, and publishes the proof as a 14-line sonnet whose acrostic spells the cipher. The verifier re-reads the USGS gauge log: a forged level breaks the cipher, and a sonnet lifted from another identity carries the same acrostic, so the verifier flags both at once. One river cannot serve two identities: the reading belongs to a single bank, so a farm must find new water for every fake it adds.
